result.summary: FAIL (0 BLOCKER, 1 MAJOR, 1 MINOR). AC8: all-hidden page ({[], nil}, equal to an empty schema), V/H boundary matrix at page_size 1 and 2, cursor-decode test, 1100-row and 250/V/250 long hidden runs. AC10: repro describe seeds (b, p) in A's schema, caller is TENANT_ADMIN of A (non-party), expects the 404 path; party controls (a,b)/(b,a) expect 200. REVERTED PINNING TESTS: git diff origin/main on test/ touches only promotion_context_allowlist_test.exs and promotion_context_entries_scope_test.exs (plus the new repro/store tests and specs); promotion_context_shaping_test.exs and promotions_test.exs are byte-identical to origin/main. MUTANTS I APPLIED MYSELF (each alone, run, then git checkout of the file): (1) N10b, tolerant_plan/1 body replaced by Jason.decode!(text) in lib/letflow/routers/promotions.ex: repro file 35/36 (--exclude long_hidden_run), 1 failed = 'the operator reads /:id and /:id/context of unparseable rows: 200, never a 500' -> KILLED, as claimed. (2) AC8 scan-cap mutant (promotion_review_store.ex scan_visible_reviews: the short-chunk clause replaced by `true -> acc`, i.e. only the first 100-row chunk is ever scanned): --only long_hidden_run 0/2 passed, both 1(e) tests failed -> KILLED, as claimed for N12. (3) AC3 request-decides mutant (review_read_access/2 {:tenant,_} branch: when query param tenant_id is a binary, the auth_context tenant_id used for the party comparison is replaced by it): repro file 36/36 PASSED, 2 excluded -> SURVIVED. The spec/handoff claim that T5 kills N3 is not reproduced by this mutant form. Probe (temporary copy of the file, deleted afterwards, never committed): changing the T5 first-half attack to name the STORED foreign tenant id (ctx.b) instead of the reader's own tenant makes the test pass on clean lib (2/2) and fail under the mutant (1/2) -> the discriminating attack is simply absent from the committed T5. REVERT VERIFIED: git status --porcelain lib/ test/ is empty and git diff HEAD -- lib is 0 bytes after every mutant; the repro file re-ran green after the last revert ('Result: 38 passed'). No erl/mix processes of mine left. Note: another mix test invocation of a sibling was connected to the same DB during my first run (TenantSchemaReaper deferral log); no effect on results.

issues.description: T5 'request params and headers naming the reader's tenant do not open a non-party review' (promotion_read_stored_ids_test.exs ~line 336) puts the READER's own tenant id (ctx.a) in tenant_id/source_tenant_id/target_tenant_id/tenant/tenantId and x-tenant-id/x-letflow-tenant, against a (b, p) review whose stored ids are b and p. An implementation that lets a request tenant_id param replace the authenticated tenant in the party comparison is not caught, because the request value (a) matches neither stored id. The attack that matters is a request naming the STORED foreign id (b or p) so that it would match the review: that is never sent for the non-party half. The second half names b only against a party (a, b) review, where the party verdict is :own_side either way, so it cannot discriminate either. Mutant applied and measured: 36/36 passed (survived). A probe naming ctx.b in the first half kills it (1 of 2 failed).
issues.route_to: ELIXIR-DEV (no separate TEST-DESIGNER): in T5 first half send each of ctx.b.tenant_id and ctx.p.tenant_id (the stored source and target ids) in every param/header, for both suffixes and the list (non-party review must stay 404 / omitted). Optionally also a (b, p) review with target = reader to show a foreign-named request cannot flip a party review to :none. Then re-run, and re-apply the request-decides mutant to confirm it is killed.

issues.description: The list route has no 404 (AC4 says 'same status and body ... on all three routes'); the committed test compares the list-with-hidden-rows against the list-without byte for byte on a cursor-less page and on status+headers+items for a cursor page. That is a reasonable reading and is accepted; the cursor-page case does not compare next_cursor value (only that both are binary), which is acceptable because the cursor legitimately encodes the last emitted row and 1(d) checks it never encodes a hidden row.

result.next_action: ORCH: route back to ELIXIR-DEV to strengthen T5 (name the stored foreign ids in the request), then re-run TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR step 05b r2 (one mutant re-application suffices) before RELEASE-VALIDATOR.
